extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders (employers, labor representatives, safety professionals, and members of the public) interested in commenting on OSHA deregulatory proposed rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Information and procedural guidance for viewing OSHA's deregulatory proposed rulemakings and submitting public comments or participating in hearings. Includes docket identifiers, Federal Register links, comment deadlines, and references to procedural resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to view proposed rulemakings
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulemakings are available for viewing at the Federal Register links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided Federal Register link for each Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (listed under 'Federal Register Link') to read the full proposed regulatory text, summaries, and any published schedules or hearing notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how to submit public comments
rubrics_metrics.description: All public comments are accessible on regulations.gov. Each rule entry on the page includes a 'Docket Link (Comment Submission)' pointing to the regulations.gov docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments via the docket link provided (regulations.gov). Ensure you select or reference the correct docket (e.g., 'OSHA-2025-0041') so your submission is associated with the intended proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period deadlines and status
rubrics_metrics.description: The comment period on OSHA's following Notices of Proposed Rulemakings ended on September 2, 2025: Open Fires in Marine Terminals, House Falls in Marine Terminals, and Safety Color Code... The comment period for all other proposed rulemakings concluded on November 1, 2025. Deadline for comments: Closed for Comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be submitted within the published comment period to be considered. Confirm the specific deadline for each docket via the Federal Register or regulations.gov; once closed, the page indicates comments are no longer being accepted for these items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing participation (NOITA requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If OSHA holds a public hearing, the schedule and detailed participation information, including instructions for submitting Notices of Intention to Appear (NOITA) for those wishing to speak or ask questions, will be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor the Federal Register entry for the rule for any announced hearings and the specific procedures and deadlines for submitting a NOITA if you intend to appear or question witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use OSHA's rulemaking process resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information on OSHA's rulemaking process and how stakeholders can participate is available at https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/rulemakingprocess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult OSHA's rulemaking process page for broader procedural guidance (how rulemakings proceed, how public input is used, forms of participation, timelines) before preparing comments or planning participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify rules by Document ID, RIN, and Document Citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each listed proposed rule includes identifiers: Document ID (e.g., OSHA-2025-0041-0002), RIN (e.g., 1218-AD71), and Document Citation (e.g., 90 FR 28370).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing comments or inquiries, reference the exact Document ID, RIN, and/or Document Citation shown on the page so your submission or correspondence clearly identifies the targeted proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and use the rule 'Summary' to focus comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry includes a 'Summary' that describes the proposed change (for example: 'OSHA proposes to clarify its interpretation of the General Duty Clause...'; 'OSHA proposes to remove some medical evaluation requirements...'; 'The proposed rule revises some substance-specific respirator requirements...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the summary to understand the scope and intent of the proposal and to frame comments on relevant aspects (legal interpretation, scope of change, affected provisions, anticipated impacts). Consult the full Federal Register notice for regulatory text and supporting analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of rescissions, removals, and alignment actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Several proposals would remove or rescind standards from the CFR (e.g., 'House Falls in Marine Terminals', 'Open Fires in Marine Terminals', 'Safety Color Code for Marking Physical Hazards') or align substance-specific standards with the Respiratory Protection standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commenting on rescissions or removals, address potential regulatory gaps, consequences for affected workplaces, and whether alignment with other standards adequately preserves protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawn/terminated rulemakings and their effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: 'Withdrawal of the proposal does not change any employer's obligation to complete and retain occupational injury and illness records under OSHA's regulations. Withdrawal of the proposal also does not change the recording criteria or definitions used for these records.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that a withdrawn proposal does not alter current legal obligations; comments discussing withdrawn items should acknowledge the current regulatory status and any continuing compliance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor page 'related links' for ongoing updates
rubrics_metrics.description: For ongoing updates and further information, stakeholders are encouraged to utilize the related links provided on the webpage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly check the OSHA webpage, Federal Register entries, and docket pages on regulations.gov for updates, corrections, hearing notices, and new submission opportunities related to these deregulatory rulemakings.
